posts.title: The songs that raised us
posts.body:
My mother had three cassettes in the car and no interest in adding a fourth: Mahmoud Ahmed, Aster Aweke and a tizita mixtape with a hand-written label. I spent years thinking that was a limitation. Now I understand it was an education.

Tizita does something no other music does for me — it makes missing something feel like a place you can visit rather than a wound you carry. What is the song that takes you straight back to a room you have not stood in for years?

author.bio: Reader, reviewer, and collector of quotations. Ask me for a recommendation.

category.description: Tizita on a Sunday, azmari nights, new releases and the songs that carry a whole decade. What is on repeat for you, and who should we be listening to?

posts.title: Five Ethiopian albums for a long drive
posts.body:
A friend asked me for a road-trip playlist and I sent back a lecture. Passing it on, shortened: one album for the first hour while the city is still behind you, one for the mountain stretch where the radio dies, one for when everyone is asleep except the driver, one for the last thirty minutes, and one you save for the arrival.

The rule is simple — no skipping. An album is a conversation, not a shuffle.

author.bio: Football obsessive. Weekend runner. I will argue about tactics for hours.
